The divergent rank-one term contributes one mode; compression of the remaining finite form to 1-perp yields -2D-I-A^-1, and path resistance D_ij=(e_i-e_j)^T L^+(e_i-e_j) gives 4L^+-I-A^-1. Strict crossings exclude zero threshold directions, the Jacobi recurrence gives simplicity, and free tails rule out in-band localized eigenfunctions. originality.rationale: PASS (best-of-knowledge, with specified residual risks). Equivalent formulations include the number of isolated eigenvalues above [0,4] of a finite-rank positive bond perturbation, Birman-Schwinger positive inertia at the band edge, and Dirichlet-to-Neumann/transfer-matrix threshold counting. None of the specifically inspected historical cases treats the all-p weighted-path inverse formula. The general resolvent principle and effective resistance identities are standard and stronger frameworks; they must be combined with this particular one-dimensional band-edge compression and all-gap inertia. No inspected published all-p theorem was found that already supplies the precise count, but broad lattice perturbation literature remains a risk. General bounds or two-particle experiments do not imply exact all-p staircase. Conversely, p=2 is implied by new p>=2 formula and is not claimed separately.
residual_risks: Unindexed older 1D transfer-matrix/spectral shift analyses may already contain an equivalent all-p inertia theorem.

An all-p, arbitrary-gap-and-contrast exact localized-mode count for the canonical discrete harmonic chain is a meaningful structural spectral result; the band-edge equality law and complete mode staircase supply information not obtainable from a few isolated-defect calculations. A practical researcher can determine whether each additional stiff bond produces a bound mode without numerically resolving arbitrarily near-edge eigenvalues.
